resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO), Residential Change of Tenant/Occupancy/Ownership inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Florence Township Housing Department (Construction and Code Enforcement)
resale_co.lead_time: Allow at least 2 weeks to get the first inspection appointment; in busy times it can be up to 4 weeks out.
requirements: Smoke alarms on every level and outside each sleeping area; replace alarms older than 10 years; battery units must be 10-year sealed (UL 217)
Carbon monoxide alarm near the bedrooms if the home has fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Portable fire extinguisher (Township Code 116-4.B(1)(d)), see fire certificate section
Electrical: 100 amp minimum service, grounded outlets with cover plates, GFI outlets in bathrooms, panel door with no open slots
Plumbing: no leaks, J-bend sink drains, water heater relief pipe to 6 inches above floor, hot water 120 to 140 degrees, backflow devices where needed
Sump pump works, drains properly and opening is covered
Floors, walls and ceilings sound with no holes, trip hazards or loose paint
Kitchen: stove, oven and broiler work; anti-tilt bracket on range
Windows open, stay open and lock; screens on all windows; no broken glass
Doors latch; exterior and bathroom doors lock; garage door and opener work safely
Graspable handrails on stairs; deck and porch railings at 30 inches or more with no more than 4 inch openings
Roof certification from a licensed roofer if there are signs of active leaks
Exterior, gutters, downspouts, fences, sidewalks and driveway in good repair; yard mowed and cleared
Heating system certification on the Township form, original with raised seal (not needed for Florence Tollgate condos); inactive oil fill pipes and tanks removed
Level II chimney certification for wood-burning fireplaces or solid fuel stoves; any work done without permits must be permitted and inspected

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out page 1 of the Housing Inspection Application form (check Buyer, give owner and buyer contact details) and submit it with the fee to the Florence Township Housing Department, 711 Broad Street, Florence. The inspection is booked for the next open slot once the form is complete and paid. A lock box is allowed for vacant homes; otherwise an adult must let the inspector in. Give at least 24 hours notice to cancel or reschedule. For an as-is sale where the buyer will not move in, ask for a notarized "No Occupancy" letter (needs the paid application, the as-is contract and a signed buyer letter).

resale_co.notes: Re-check 2026-10-13: the live florence-nj.gov pages and the July 2025 Housing Inspection Application form now open normally, so they are cited directly instead of Internet Archive copies; the wording, staff and fees are unchanged. The Township Code was read on ecode360 this time. Section 116-4 (last amended December 3, 2025 by Ord. No. 2025-26) bars anyone from buying, selling or transferring a residential unit unless a CCO is first obtained, and says a CCO is granted or denied within 10 business days of the application. Chapter 2, Schedule A (last amended September 4, 2024 by Ord. No. 2024-16) lists the same $165 initial inspection and $35 / $50 / $75 / $100 re-inspection fees as the form, plus a $20 fee for amending a CCO. Conflict: the form and the code both describe a notarized 'No Occupancy' letter for as-is purchases, but the form says the application and $165.00 fee must be paid first, while Section 116-4B(1)(o) of the code says a '$60 inspection fee'; the form's $165.00 is listed here and the difference is an open question. Section 116-4A also ends with the words 'and shall only occur while the subject property is not currently occupied'; the application page says vacancy is required for rental inspections, so ask whether an occupied home can be inspected for a sale. A 90-day validity is stated only for rental inspections done before a tenant is named; no validity period is published for sales. The Township does not issue a Temporary CO. Other staff on the housing page: Jessica Carroll, Code Enforcement Officer, ext. 118, jcarroll@florence-nj.gov; Shannyn Jones, Technical Assistant, ext. 117 (techassist@florence-nj.gov); Jodie Hein, Technical Assistant, ext. 131 (techassist2@florence-nj.gov). The general Township line is (609) 499-2525. Rentals also need Landlord and Tenant Registration forms and a Lead-Safe Certificate for pre-1978 units ($40 Township filing fee), and the form's water meter letter says a new radio water meter must be installed after a housing inspection for a rental unit before the CCO is issued.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level (including habitable attic and basement) and outside each sleeping area; alarms must be replaced after 10 years
Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed, single station, listed to UL 217; hard-wired alarms from original construction may not be swapped for battery units
Carbon monoxide alarm (UL 2034) in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms when the home has fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Portable fire extinguisher still required by Township Code 116-4.B(1)(d) (re-adopted in the December 2025 amendment) and the July 2025 form: at least 2A:10B:C, residential rated, 10 lb or less
Extinguisher mounted with the maker's bracket, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, visible, near an exit path
Extinguisher serviced and tagged by a certified contractor within 12 months, or a receipt for a newly bought unit; owner's manual present; do not remove the tamper seal

authorities.how_to_apply: No separate application found. The smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher check is part of the Housing Inspection Application for the CCO, submitted with the fee to the Housing Department at 711 Broad Street.

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Florence Township's fire code enforcing agency as a fire district (code D), and the DCA directory names Fire Official Brian Richardson (Florence Twp Fire Dept / Fire District, 401 Firehouse Lane, phone (609) 499-1393, brichardson@ftfd40.org). But the same directory page lists 'Florence Twp Constr Dept' at 711 Broad Street, (609) 499-2130 as the Smoke Detector Compliance contact, and the fire district's own Fire Prevention page (now readable live) says the Bureau enforces the fire code 'in all buildings except 1 and 2 family owner occupied dwellings'. The Township's CCO form and Code Section 116-4 cover smoke, CO and extinguisher as part of the housing inspection. So for a home sale, go through the Township Housing Department. New on 2026-10-13: Township Code Section 76-12D (fire prevention chapter, last amended 2005) still sets a separate fee schedule for a 'certificate of smoke detector/CO detector compliance as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70:2.3' ($40 / $50 / $75 / $125, tiered by days before it is needed). It is listed as a second, low-confidence authority because no current page says the fire district issues resale certificates for 1-2 family homes, and these old fees are below the current state fees; confirm with the Housing Department which office issues the certificate and whether any separate fee applies. The Township still requires an extinguisher under its own code even though P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state rule. Township Code 76-12D still lists an older smoke/CO certificate fee schedule ($40 / $50 / $75 / $125, last amended 2005) that no current Township page or form uses.

other_items.label: Open permits and unpermitted work
other_items.detail: Property records are checked. Any work done without a permit must get a permit and pass inspection, and outstanding construction permits must be closed, before the CCO is issued.

other_items.label: Heating system certification
other_items.detail: Original Township Heating System Certification form signed by a licensed contractor with raised seal; copies or faxes not accepted.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Level II chimney certification for wood-burning fireplaces or solid fuel stoves.

other_items.label: Age Restricted Development form
other_items.detail: Required if applicable, listed with the CCO application.

other_items.label: Underground oil tank
other_items.detail: Township FAQ says a tank in use and not leaking, or properly abandoned in place with permits, may stay; removal is a buyer/seller negotiation.

other_items.label: Sidewalk repairs before sale
other_items.detail: Township Code 116-13B(9) says deteriorated, uprooted, cracked or dilapidated sidewalks must be repaired by the owner prior to sale or rental (sidewalks are also on the CCO checklist).

open_questions: Whether the Township issues a separate state smoke/CO certificate document or the CCO covers it, and whether the fire district fee schedule in Code 76-12D ($40 to $125) is still used for any home sales.
'No Occupancy' letter fee: the July 2025 form says the $165.00 application fee must be paid first, while Code 116-4B(1)(o) (amended December 2025) says a $60 inspection fee.
Whether an occupied home can be inspected for a sale (Code 116-4A says the CCO 'shall only occur while the subject property is not currently occupied').
No-show or late cancellation fee amount: the FAQ warns of fees for cancelling with less than 24 hours notice but no amount was found.
Payment methods accepted are not stated on the pages found.
